title:
Ukraine Says It Sank a Russian Warship.
COP31 Ends Without a Deal.
Asia Moves to Steady Markets.
subject: Ukraine Says It Sank a Russian Warship in Libya. COP31 Ends Without a Deal. Asia Moves to Steady Markets.
preview_text: A far-flung strike, a stalled climate summit, market rescues, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
description: Zelensky says Ukrainian sea drones sank a Russian corvette in Libya, Asian regulators act to calm markets and the US probes an Nvidia-linked firm.
contents_extra: Why COP31 failed, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Ukraine Says Its Sea Drones Sank a Russian Warship in Libya
paragraphs: The BBC reports President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian drones sank a Russian warship at a port in Libya. Zelensky wrote that seven naval drones targeted the corvette Merkury on Sunday. He said a Ka-27 helicopter was also destroyed. He called it an exemplary Ukrainian operation, the BBC says.

The Guardian reports the Merkury had stopped in Benghazi to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials. Satellite imagery showed it had sunk, more than 1,000 miles from south Ukraine. The UN mission in Libya called for an independent investigation. Benghazi is controlled by forces aligned with Russia, the paper says.

stories.title: Asian Governments Move to Steady Sliding Stock Markets
paragraphs: CNBC reports South Korea, China and Taiwan have introduced new measures to support their markets. Seoul said on Sunday it would prepare a stabilization fund worth 10.76 trillion won for immediate activation. Taiwan banned short selling below the previous close. Beijing will let investors borrow more for stock purchases from Nov. 30.

The BBC reports that worries about an AI crash are growing in San Francisco, the heart of the AI boom. One AI worker told the BBC he is certain a crash is coming. Some factors suggest any downturn may hit the city more softly than feared, the BBC says. AI firms employ relatively few workers there, the BBC says.

stories.title: US Probes a Singapore Firm Linked to the Nvidia Chip Case
paragraphs: CNBC reports Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said the US is investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed. Megaspeed is a Singapore-based firm running data centers across Southeast Asia. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday the administration was seeking answers from Nvidia about chip sales to China. Megaspeed says it is a lawful business.

CNBC reports Nvidia shares rose 8.6% in premarket trading on Monday after a more than 40% slump over the past month. Anthropic was up 4.47% at 5:21 a.m. ET. The Nasdaq slid 10% last week, CNBC says. These were pre-market moves before Monday's US open.

deep_dive.title: Why the Longest UN Climate Talks Ended Without a Deal
paragraphs: The BBC reports countries failed to reach a major new climate deal at the COP31 talks in Turkey. Negotiations were due to end on Friday but ran into Sunday. That made it the longest UN climate conference in history. The final text did not directly mention fossil fuels, which the EU and Pacific island nations found unacceptable.

CNBC reports Ireland's climate minister Darragh O'Brien, speaking for the EU, said some oil states hijacked the conference. He made the remark when asked by Reuters about Saudi Arabia's role. Saudi delegate Mohammad Ayoub said Arab countries engaged in good faith, the BBC reports. Bahamas Prime Minister Philip Davis said Antalya exhausted small island states' patience.

The BBC's climate team says the summit's central agreement, the Antalya Pacts, could not bridge the divide on fossil fuels. The same pledge had been made three years earlier at COP28 in Dubai. Rich nations also did not put a figure on adaptation money for developing countries. The BBC calls it a serious blow to multilateralism.

Some work still moved forward. More than 90 countries signed a pledge to raise electrification to 35% by 2035 from about 23% today, CNBC reports, citing Australia's Chris Bowen. Countries also agreed to advance a just transition framework for workers, the BBC says. UN chief Antonio Guterres said he was deeply disappointed no consensus was reached.

trivia.question: How many naval drones does Zelensky say Ukraine deployed against the Russian corvette Merkury?
trivia.explanation: The answer is seven. The BBC reports Zelensky wrote that seven naval drones were deployed to target and sink the Merkury.

poll.question: Can UN climate summits still deliver global deals?

World view: Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore full diplomatic ties, the BBC reports the leaders met in Oyo, Congo-Brazzaville, on Sunday.
A report says Israel's destruction of Gaza has left a toxic wasteland, the Guardian reports on findings by Oxfam and Ceobs.
Spain's far-right Vox is on course for almost 20% of the vote, the Guardian reports the party won 0.2% in 2016.
Need to know: Yemen's Houthis claim an attack on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery, CNBC reports the extent of any damage remains unclear.
Israel's opposition leader condemns settler arson attacks as Jewish terrorism, the Guardian reports at least four West Bank communities were attacked.
A boy, 7, is rescued from rubble near Kyiv, the BBC reports officials said Russian strikes on Dymer killed 11 people.
Money & markets: Tata Steel shares slide after a $1.67 billion APL Apollo deal, CNBC reports APL Apollo's stock fell more than 19%.
French biotech Abivax rejects a short seller's claims, CNBC reports its shares rose 10% in Monday morning trading.
Compass Group plans to move its main listing to the US, the BBC reports, citing a source close to the company.
Future frontiers: US intelligence chief warns of more tech bumps, CNBC reports Jay Clayton said system upgrades may bring temporary interruptions.
Robot startup Foundation ends staff health coverage, CNBC reports, citing a memo it obtained.
A psychologist debunks the idea that we use only 10% of our brains, the Guardian reports she is shocked the myth persists.
The score: Carlos Alcaraz wins his first ATP Finals title, BBC Sport reports he beat world number one Alexander Zverev.
Diego Simeone breaks the record for La Liga wins, BBC Sport reports Atletico beat Getafe 3-0 for his 345th.
The 49ers win in Mexico City to reach 9-1, BBC Sport reports 85,612 fans watched at the Azteca.
Life & culture: Chamonix plans visitor quotas for Lac Blanc, the Guardian reports up to 4,000 tourists a day visit in summer.
Up to 1.1m people may join a Jetstar refund class action, the Guardian reports a trial may come in March 2027.
Queensland families revolt over a $5 gate fee at kids' football, the Guardian reports clubs are preparing to break away.
